title: The Wedding at Cana
source: Musée du Louvre, Paris (public domain: Veronese died in 1588). Wikimedia Commons: Les Noces de Cana - Paolo Veronese - Musée du Louvre Peintures INV 142 ; MR 384.jpg, 10068x6742, saved at 8000 px.
caption: Millions walk past it to see the Mona Lisa. Almost nobody stops. #art #arthistory #painting #louvre #museum
_verify: VERIFIED 2026-10-12 (web search: NYRB/Saltzman, TheCollector, Louvre-related sources): 1563, painted for the refectory of San Giorgio Maggiore, Venice; taken by Napoleon's troops 1797, arrived in Paris 1798; in 1815 Vivant Denon convinced the Austrians it was too large to move; hangs in the Salle des États opposite the Mona Lisa.
Commonly cited, not checked against the Louvre: 'largest painting in the Louvre', about 6.77 x 9.94 m, more than 130 figures.
Musicians as Veronese (white), Titian (red), Tintoretto, Bassano: a tradition from Boschini (17th c.), sources disagree on who plays what. Slide says 'Tradition says'.
Visible on the image: the hourglass on the musicians' table, the servant pouring red wine from the stone jar, the man with the cleaver above Christ, the man studying his glass.
Cleaver as a sign of Christ's sacrifice: an interpretation, presented as 'many read it as'.
NOT used: 'Napoleon's soldiers cut it in half' (only one weak source).

slides.headline: Millions walk past this painting. Almost nobody stops.
slides.sub: Paolo Veronese, The Wedding at Cana, 1563

slides.headline: The Louvre's biggest painting
slides.text: Almost 10 metres wide, more than 130 people. It hangs right across from the Mona Lisa, behind the crowd.

slides.headline: But first, find the guest of honour
slides.text: In the middle sits Jesus, calm, his mother beside him. The wedding is in Cana. The party is pure Venice.

slides.headline: And then the wine runs out
slides.text: A servant tips a stone jar that was filled with water. What pours out is red.

slides.headline: Someone checks the miracle
slides.text: A guest in a rich robe raises his glass and stares at the new wine.

slides.headline: Meanwhile, the band plays on
slides.text: Tradition says the musicians are Venice's star painters: Veronese himself in white, Titian in red.

slides.headline: Look at their table
slides.text: Between them stands an hourglass. At the happiest party in town, time is running out.

slides.headline: Now look right above Jesus
slides.text: A man raises a cleaver over meat. Many read it as a warning: the lamb will be sacrificed.

slides.headline: Taken by Napoleon
slides.text: In 1797 his soldiers carried it off from Venice. In 1815 the Louvre said it was too big to send back. It's still here.
